# Blender Pipeline

## Principle

**Every runtime 3D asset in Magnet Rush is generated by script.** There are no
hand-authored `.blend` files, and no manual export step. The art source of
truth is Python, so assets are diffable, reviewable, reproducible on any
machine, and regenerable in one command.

## Toolchain

| | |
|---|---|
| Blender | 5.2.0 LTS (`C:\Program Files\Blender Foundation\Blender 5.2\blender.exe`) |
| Blender Python | 3.13.13 |
| Mode | headless (`--background`), no GUI, no interaction |
| Output | GLB (binary glTF 2.0) in `assets/models/` |

### A note on Blender MCP

The brief specified authoring through Blender MCP. **No Blender MCP server was
connected to this session** — the only MCP servers available were Apollo.io,
Figma, Canva, Google Drive and Notion. Blender itself *was* installed, so the
pipeline drives it headlessly through its Python API instead.

This meets the brief's actual requirement — assets are modelled, exported and
integrated automatically, with nothing handed back for manual modelling — and
is strictly better for a production project, because a script in the repo is
reproducible where a sequence of live MCP calls is not. If a Blender MCP server
is connected later, it can drive these same `mr_kit` helpers.

## Layout

```
art/blender/
  mr_kit.py              shared kit: palette, materials, primitives, export
  build_assets.py        asset definitions, grouped; the entry point
  write_manifest_md.py   asset_index.json -> docs/asset_manifest.md
  asset_index.json       generated index (tri counts, sizes, budgets)
assets/models/
  core/  metal/  platforms/  obstacles/
```

## Commands

```sh
# everything
blender --background --python art/blender/build_assets.py

# one or more groups
blender --background --python art/blender/build_assets.py -- core metal

# refresh the human-readable manifest
python art/blender/write_manifest_md.py
```

The build **fails with a non-zero exit code if any asset exceeds its triangle
budget**, so the budgets in the brief are enforced by CI rather than by
convention.

## The kit (`mr_kit.py`)

**Palette.** The art bible's colour roles are constants (`CYAN`, `CORE_BLUE`,
`SILVER`, `CHARCOAL`, `ORANGE`, `GREEN`, …). Assets reference roles, never raw
values, so a palette change is one edit.

**Materials.** `material()` builds a Principled BSDF and caches it by name, so
repeated props share one material instance and the exported scene keeps its
material count low. The cache is cleared by `reset_scene()`, since reloading the
file frees every datablock.

**Primitives.** All low-poly by construction: `box`, `icosphere`, `cylinder`,
`cone`, `torus`, `gear`, `crystal`, `bevel_plate`. `crystal()` is the signature
one — an icosphere with per-vertex radial jitter, flat-shaded, which produces
the faceted energy-crystal silhouette the Kanban Core needs.

**Composition.** `join()` merges objects into a single mesh while remapping
material indices, so a multi-part prop still exports as one primitive per
material rather than a node hierarchy.

**Export.** `export_glb()` recalculates normals, applies transforms, exports the
selection as GLB, and returns a manifest record (triangles, materials, bytes).

## Conventions enforced in code

* metric scale, 1 unit = 1 metre
* transforms applied — every mesh exports at identity
* normals recalculated outward
* **flat shading everywhere** — the faceted look is the art direction, and it
  also lets the swarm batcher stamp templates without smoothing artefacts
* pivots at the logical centre of rotation
* **no textures at all** — flat colour plus emission. This keeps the APK small
  and sidesteps texture-compression format fragmentation (ETC2 vs ASTC vs BC)
  across Android GPUs entirely.

## Relationship to the swarm batcher

Swarm-class assets are not only loaded as GLB nodes. Their geometry is also
consumed as CPU-side templates by the batcher described in
`docs/renderer_decision.md`, which stamps them through per-object transforms
into a single merged mesh. That is why swarm pieces carry the tightest budget
(≤500 triangles, most are 12–44): those counts are multiplied by up to ~220
concurrent objects every frame.

## Current output

54 assets, 7,124 triangles, ~481 KB total, 0 budget violations. Full table in
`docs/asset_manifest.md`.

Verified end-to-end on an Android device build: `assets/models/core/kanban_core.glb`
loads via `Node.fromGlbAsset` and renders through Impeller, with the HUD
reporting `core: BLENDER GLB`.

## Remaining groups

The obstacle, enemy and boss libraries in sections 8–10 of the brief are not yet
generated. They extend `build_assets.py` with additional `build_*` functions and
a `GROUPS` entry — no new infrastructure is required. See
`docs/known_limitations.md`.
